items.name: SpendQuery
items.summary: Plain-English search over 100M+ federal, state and city spending records. Government contractors use it to find open bids, see contracts coming up for re-bid and size up the competition.
highlights: DuckDB and dbt platform loading USAspending.gov, SAM.gov and 16 state checkbooks, each state year reconciled to the cent
A semantic layer turns questions into a validated query plan, never raw SQL, and serves the web app, API and an MCP server
Slowest endpoint cut from 43 s to 0.2 s; 257 API tests plus browser tests and live comparisons against USAspending.gov

items.name: PaakData
items.summary: AI-first stock analytics for 12,000+ US stocks and ETFs. Ask in plain English and get exact screens back, with the filters shown so every answer can be checked.
highlights: Natural-language screening over hundreds of data fields
MCP server so assistants like Claude can screen stocks and pull company briefs directly
LLM and RAG pipelines that write company briefs with data-quality warnings built in, plus catalyst-based “similar to” search

items.name: AskEider
items.summary: Privacy-first natural-language analytics on a governed semantic layer. The model never sees your schema, values or rows; every answer comes from governed metric definitions.
highlights: A local resolver maps schema-free intent to metrics; MetricFlow compiles the SQL and DuckDB runs it read-only in a sandbox
Profiles any DuckDB, Parquet, CSV, SQLite, Postgres or MySQL source and generates a working dbt + MetricFlow layer
REST API, Python and TypeScript SDKs, MCP server, Slack and Teams apps; 450+ tests and an OWASP LLM Top 10 threat model

items.name: MLCompass
items.summary: Bring a dataset; MLCompass recommends which kind of machine learning fits it, then trains, checks and explains the model end to end. Built for people who know their data but not ML, every result comes with a plain-language answer and a trust verdict.
highlights: Guide me turns four plain questions into a validated model. It ranks 10 ML approaches, applies leakage and baseline checks, explains predictions with SHAP and “what would change the outcome?”, and runs an Autopilot that keeps only gains that hold up under cross-validation.

Marketing measurement: a marketing mix model that captures paid media’s halo on direct and organic traffic (within 9.7% of known effects, against 12.3% for last-click), synthetic-control geo experiments, and Shapley + ML attribution that scales to 500K journeys.

Works with any AI model, or none: an agent that runs only tested tools and never generated code, and summaries written for executives, marketing, finance and sales. Exports a prediction API, a training script, and Snowflake and Databricks deployment kits, with 343 tests.

items.name: MCP Browser
items.summary: The search engine that shows its work. An open-source AI search browser that sends each question to the few MCP servers that know the answer, chosen from the 48,000+ in the official MCP Registry, and shows several independent sources side by side instead of one generated answer. Runs locally with no account, and works without an AI key, with Ollama, or inside Claude.
highlights: Cross-check: checks a claim, or every fact in an AI answer, against independent sources and quotes each source's own sentence
Dependency check: reads a lockfile or a GitHub repo and compares two vulnerability databases
Tell me when: watches prices, releases and web pages, on your own computer
106 tested pipelines that chain MCP servers together
